title: Limitations on Autoregressive Token Generation via Sequential Sampling
abstract: arXiv:2610.14615v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We study autoregressive token generation through the notion of sequential samplers: A circuit that samples the next symbol only given the previous ones and possibly a small amount of state. We show that (1) a sequential sampler with $k$ bits of state can be simulated by a stateless one at a roughly $O(2^{k})$ size overhead; (2) efficient insertional sampling (Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019) is more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order; (3) sequential samplers with small state cannot establish certain forms of covert cryptographic channels. Result (1), together with the pseudoentropy vs. sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng (STOC 2012), characterizes efficient sequential sampleability with small state. Result (3) provides a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.

translated_title: 通过顺序采样实现自回归token生成的局限性
translated_abstract: 我们通过顺序采样器的概念来研究自回归token生成：顺序采样器是一种仅根据先前的符号（以及可能存在的少量状态）来采样下一个符号的电路。我们证明了：（1）具有 $k$ 比特状态的顺序采样器可以由无状态采样器以大约 $O(2^{k})$ 的大小开销来模拟；（2）高效插入式采样（Stern, Chan, Kiros, Uszkoreit, ICML 2019）比任何固定顺序的高效顺序采样都更强大；（3）小状态的顺序采样器无法建立某些形式的隐蔽密码学信道。结果（1）与Vadhan和Zheng（STOC 2012）的伪熵与顺序可采样性对偶性相结合，刻画了具有小状态的高效顺序可采样性。结果（3）为防范恶意LLM智能体之间的潜意识协调提供了一种潜在的安全机制。
tldr: 本文通过顺序采样器理论刻画了自回归token生成的根本局限，证明小状态顺序采样器可被无状态采样器以指数开销模拟、插入式采样严格强于固定顺序采样、且小状态采样器无法建立隐蔽密码信道，从而为防御恶意LLM智能体间的隐秘协调提供了潜在的安全机制。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes fundamental limitations of autoregressive token generation via sequential sampling, proving that small-state sequential samplers can be simulated by stateless ones with roughly $O(2^k)$ overhead, that efficient insertional sampling is strictly more powerful than efficient sequential sampling in any fixed order, and that small-state samplers cannot establish certain covert cryptographic channels—offering a potential safety mechanism against subliminal coordination among malicious LLM agents.
